summary: Wrote, fact-checked and rendered stills for L-20261028-01, 'How airlines really make money (it isn't the seats)' (8:13, 119 beats), from Scout's top topic, but marked it failed: QA still found scene-code bugs after the two allowed fix rounds.
why: 1 of 3 long videos this week, so a video was due. Number check passed and fact review passed after 1 rewrite. Every render gate passed. QA failed three times; the last failure was all scene code Studio may not change: the build camera crops actors headless, and Rohan's facepalm pose puts his phone over his face. The rule is two QA fix rounds, and a failed long video beats a bad one shipped.

findings.title: Fact review: 1 rewrite
findings.detail: Failed first because Sharma spoke as a banker who signed miles deals, and because a line told the viewer to 'do the sum'. Both were fixed (plus a gate-coffee price, 'by morning' parcels and a Hindi word), then it passed.

findings.title: QA review: 3 rounds, failed
findings.detail: Round 1 failed on 8 points, all fixed: hook tag under the captions, two count-ups cut off, a stale HUD counter, text over text, Rohan cut off, a repeated grid thumbnail and a chart callout. Round 2 failed because build-beat camera framing crops the cast, plus phone-over-face and the jet's BANK label. Round 3: the same scene bugs remain.

findings.title: Gates hit along the way
findings.detail: Literal-action rule (9 beats), 2.5 s visual gaps (case beats can't pass it past about 4 s; the gate prints only the worst gap), labels and tags off-frame on close-ups, and 16% empty stills. All fixed in the script and logged in the backlog.
